problem: Modular EIF systems on ALFRED either need extra training data (e.g. a CNN semantic search trained on dedicated object-location annotations) or ignore the robot's physical constraints (agent size, camera pose, reach), causing collisions and failed interactions.
motivation: Data-hungry modules negate the sample efficiency of modular approaches and are prone to simulator bias. Physical constraints are easy to obtain for any robot, so explicit use should help performance and cross-robot portability, while pretrained LLMs can supply object-landmark commonsense zero-shot.
key_idea: Extend a FILM-style modular EIF pipeline with explicitly configured physical constraints (obstacle inflation, camera pose, reach, interaction offset) and replace the trained landmark-based semantic search CNN with zero-shot LLM prompting for collocation probabilities.
insight: Most of the gain comes from correct physical-constraint use: the ablation shows obstacle enlargement of 10 cm instead of 20 cm drops val-unseen SR from 50.18 to 28.87, and collisions fall from 11.00% to 0.24% of failures vs FILM. LLM-prompted search matches the trained CNN (SR 50.18 vs 50.67) and is only modestly above random search (48.21), so its value is data-efficiency and extensibility rather than accuracy, and small iTHOR rooms may not sufficiently penalize poor search.
method: Perception (from FILM, unchanged): BERT-based language module maps instructions to templated object-action subtask sequences; UNet depth plus Mask R-CNN segmentation build a top-down semantic map (5 cm cells).

Motion controller: deterministic selection among local adjustment (target in view), semantic map lookup (target in map), and semantic search (otherwise); a navigation module then plans a collision-free path.

Local adjustment with physical constraints: uses camera height 1.6 m and pose to correct depth-based relative position, checks reach within 1.5 m, and positions the agent 50 cm from the target for OpenObject to avoid interference from the deformed object.
Navigation: inflates the obstacle map by the agent radius (20 cm cylinder) so the agent can be treated as a point in shortest-path planning.

LLM semantic search: p(e_t)=sum_l p(e_t|e_l)p(e_l), with the collocation probability from GPT-Neo via the template 'If I can search from [LANDMARKS], I might find [target] [in/on] [landmark]', with 10 in-context sample pairs using non-ALFRED objects.
Prompt robustness: landmark and sample order are randomized and the result is averaged over 20 runs; landmarks are the receptacle-category objects.

setting.backbone: FILM perception (BERT language, UNet depth, Mask R-CNN segmentation, trained on ALFRED) + rule-based controller + GPT-Neo (frozen, prompted)
setting.training_data: Perception modules trained on ALFRED data (reused from FILM/HLSM/ALFWorld); no extra data for the LLM search (zero-shot prompting) or controller
setting.observation: egocentric RGB with camera pose sensor readings (depth estimated from RGB)
setting.action_space: ALFRED low-level actions: RotateRight/Left, MoveAhead, LookUp/Down and interaction actions (Pickup, Put, Open, Close, Toggle, Slice) with an object mask

numbers.extra: Lower of the two leaderboard scores reported (the higher run used ALFRED-specific domain knowledge)

results: Prompter reaches 41.53% (high-level only) and 45.32% (step-by-step + high-level) SR on ALFRED test-unseen, beating the previous SOTA (EPA 36.07 and LGS-RPA 35.41) by 5.46 and 9.91 points. It also has far better path-length-weighted metrics than EPA. It trails E.T./LWIT only on test-seen PLW metrics, which the authors attribute to overfitting.
limitations: Templated language processing fixed at episode start cannot insert OpenObject for hidden objects and drops object attributes
LLM prompting is sensitive to handcrafted prompts, prepositions, landmark selection and object renaming
iTHOR rooms are small, so search-module differences are poorly measured and sim-to-real gaps may be underestimated; perception (vision) remains the main bottleneck
